title: Support for more verbs
description:
Hello, I have started to use duckplyr recently and would like to know if there are plans to implement some other functions.

I encountered the issue that `nrow()` and `ncol()` are not supported as explained on the [tidyverse website](https://duckplyr.tidyverse.org/).

I my code I have a method that extends the `dim()` function, which fixes both. Is this kind of extensions considered for the duckplyr package ?
```R
dim.prudent_duckplyr_df <- function(x) {
  n_row <- x |>
    count() |>
    unlist() |>
    unname()
  c(n_row, length(x))
}
```
I was also wondering if other functions were planned or welcomed
- Casting functions like `as.character()` or `as.numeric()` 
- Functions from `tidyr` that are supported by duckdb where a back and forth with `as_tbl()`/`pivot_*()`/`as_duckb_tibble()` does the job
- Functions from other packages used in `mutate()` like `stringr`, where duckdb function exist
- Helper functions for Rstudio that try to materialize the data for auto complete

If they are, I would be happy to suggest send suggestions.

title: `as.numeric` functions translated to CAST instead of TRY_CAST
description:
In R, `as.numerical(x)` returns a number or Na for each item in x, while in DuckDB `CAST(x AS NUMERIC)` raises an error if a value in x cannot be cast.

This results in the following, unexpected error when using duckplyr:

```R
> my_duckdb_table |> filter(is.na(as.numeric(my_char_column)))

DuckDB progress:  83%Error in `collect()`:
! Failed to collect lazy table.
Caused by error in `duckdb_result()`:
! rapi_execute: Failed to run query
Error: Conversion Error: Could not convert string "17 - 18 " to DECIMAL(18,3) when casting from source column my_char_column

LINE 3: WHERE (((CAST(my_char_columnAS NUMERIC)) IS NULL))
                 ^
Backtrace:
  1. base (local) `<fn>`(x)
  2. print.tbl_sql(x)
  3. overridePrint(o$x, o$options, o$className, o$nRow, o$nCol)
  5. dbplyr:::as.data.frame.tbl_sql(head(x, max.print))
  8. dbplyr:::collect.tbl_sql(x, n = n)
 11. dbplyr:::db_collect.DBIConnection(...)
 13. duckdb::dbSendQuery(con, sql)
 14. duckdb (local) .local(conn, statement, ...)
 15. duckdb:::duckdb_result(connection = conn, stmt_lst = stmt_lst, arrow = arrow)
```

However, if we collect first, we can do the query just fine, and filter for all rows where `my_char_column` doesn't translate to a number.

The way I see it is that Duckplyr doesn't translate `as.numeric` to something functionally equal, causing unexpected errors.

If using TRY_CAST instead of CAST in the SQL call, the two should function equally and as expected, except no warning will be emitted.

See 
 - https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/sql/expressions/cast.html#try_cast
 - https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/base/versions/3.6.2/topics/numeric

title: New behaviour of distinct + summarise in duckdb 1.5.x + duckplyr 1.2.x
description:
Hi, after updating duckdb to 1.5.x (both 1.5.0 and 1.5.1) and duckplyr to 1.2.x (both 1.2.0 and 1.2.1), some of my old code that uses `distinct` + `summarise` broke for some reason. Here is a reproducible code snippet. Do I open a separate issue in / move this issue to the duckdb repo? Thank you!

```r
library(dplyr)
library(duckplyr)

cat("R:", R.version.string, "\n")
cat("dplyr:", as.character(packageVersion("dplyr")), "\n")
cat("duckplyr:", as.character(packageVersion("duckplyr")), "\n")
cat("duckdb:", as.character(packageVersion("duckdb")), "\n\n")

src <- tibble::tibble(
  grp = c("A", "A", "A", "B", "B"),
  id = c(3L, 3L, 4L, 2L, 1L),
  barcode = c("c1", "c2", "c3", "c4", "c5"),
  n = c(1, 1, 1, 1, 1)
) |>
  duckplyr::as_duckdb_tibble()

# Expected result via eager dplyr path
expected <- src |>
  collect() |>
  distinct(id, barcode, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  summarise(.by = c(grp, id), cnt = sum(n)) |>
  left_join(
    src |>
      collect() |>
      distinct(id, barcode, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
      summarise(.by = grp, total = sum(n)),
    by = "grp"
  )

expected_rows <- nrow(expected)

run_path <- function(name, build_out) {
  out <- tryCatch(build_out(), error = function(e) e)
  
  if (inherits(out, "error")) {
    return(list(
      summary = tibble::tibble(
        path = name,
        rows = NA_integer_,
        na_grp = NA_integer_,
        na_id = NA_integer_,
        ok = FALSE,
        error = conditionMessage(out)
      ),
      out = NULL
    ))
  }
  
  rows <- nrow(out)
  na_grp <- sum(is.na(out$grp))
  na_id <- if ("id" %in% names(out)) sum(is.na(out$id)) else NA_integer_
  ok <- identical(rows, expected_rows) && na_grp == 0 && (is.na(na_id) || na_id == 0)
  
  list(
    summary = tibble::tibble(
      path = name,
      rows = rows,
      na_grp = na_grp,
      na_id = na_id,
      ok = ok,
      error = NA_character_
    ),
    out = out
  )
}

cases <- list(
  # Failing path
  "keep_all_lazy" = function() {
    x <- src |> distinct(id, barcode, .keep_all = TRUE)
    lhs <- x |> summarise(.by = c(grp, id), cnt = sum(n))
    rhs <- x |> summarise(.by = grp, total = sum(n))
    lhs |> left_join(rhs, by = "grp") |> collect()
  },
  
  # Workaround: no keep_all + additional join + re-collapse
  "no_keep_all_plus_join" = function() {
    keys <- src |> distinct(id, barcode)
    x <- keys |>
      left_join(src |> select(id, barcode, grp, n), by = c("id", "barcode")) |>
      summarise(
        .by = c(id, barcode),
        grp = first(grp),
        n = first(n)
      )
    lhs <- x |> summarise(.by = c(grp, id), cnt = sum(n))
    rhs <- x |> summarise(.by = grp, total = sum(n))
    lhs |> left_join(rhs, by = "grp") |> collect()
  },
  
  # Alternative workaround: materialise one side before join
  "keep_all_compute_rhs" = function() {
    x <- src |> distinct(id, barcode, .keep_all = TRUE)
    lhs <- x |> summarise(.by = c(grp, id), cnt = sum(n))
    rhs <- x |> summarise(.by = grp, total = sum(n)) |> compute()
    lhs |> left_join(rhs, by = "grp") |> collect()
  }
)

results <- lapply(names(cases), function(nm) run_path(nm, cases[[nm]]))
summary_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(results, `[[`, "summary"))

cat("\n=== EXPECTED (eager) ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(expected), row.names = FALSE)

for (i in seq_along(results)) {
  nm <- summary_tbl$path[i]
  out <- results[[i]]$out
  cat("\n=== ", nm, " ===\n", sep = "")
  if (is.null(out)) {
    cat("ERROR:", summary_tbl$error[i], "\n")
  } else {
    print(as.data.frame(out), row.names = FALSE)
  }
}
```

```
 <NA> NA   5     5

=== no_keep_all_plus_join ===
```

title: `duckplyr_df_from_csv`: overriding auto-detect for a single column apparently not available
description:
Attended posit::conf 2024 workshop and ran into this issue with `duckplyr_df_from_csv`: 

### Create example data 

using first three rows of IMDB data

```
myData = readr::read_tsv(
  "tconst	averageRating	numVotes
  tt0000001	5.7	2051
  tt0000002	5.7	274
  tt0000003	6.5	2005"
)
readr::write_tsv(myData, file = "ratings.tsv")
```

### Default behavior

automatic read in is fine (setting delim not required) but does not most accurately cast last column as integer

```
duckplyr_df_csv = duckplyr::duckplyr_df_from_csv(
  path = "ratings.tsv", 
  options = list(
    delim = "\t"
  )
)
```

### Manual fix

This is a correct way to read in this data, however, it requires manually re-specifying the first two column types. From https://duckdb.org/docs/data/csv/auto_detection, `types = {'numVotes': 'INTEGER'}` would be the SQL approach

```
duckplyr_df_csv = duckplyr::duckplyr_df_from_csv(
  path = "ratings.tsv",
  options = list(
    delim = "\t",
    types = list(c("VARCHAR", "DOUBLE", "INTEGER"))
  )
)
```

### Kirill's attempt

We could not find a way to specify just a single column. Here's one of Kirill's attempts:

```
duckplyr_df_csv = duckplyr::duckplyr_df_from_csv(
  path = "ratings.tsv",
  options = list(
    delim = "\t",
    types = list(list(tconst = "VARCHAR", numVotes = "INTEGER"))
  )
)
```

description:
Hi, thank you a lot for updating duckplyr to the latest version! I really appreciate it. I'm currently testing the new version with my packages, and found a new behaviour. Seems like a bug, but I'm not 100% sure.

To reproduce:

```r
library(duckplyr)
df <- data.frame(x = c(1, 2))
df <- mutate(df, y = 2)
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".parquet")
df <- compute_parquet(df, path, options = list(compression = "zstd", compression_level = 9))
```

```
! {"exception_type":"Binder","exception_message":"Invalid named parameter \"compression_level\" for function read_parquet\nCandidates:\n    binary_as_string BOOLEAN\n    can_have_nan BOOLEAN\n    compression VARCHAR\n    debug_use_openssl BOOLEAN\n    encryption_config ANY\n    explicit_cardinality UBIGINT\n    file_row_number BOOLEAN\n    filename ANY\n    hive_partitioning BOOLEAN\n    hive_types ANY\n    hive_types_autocast BOOLEAN\n    parquet_version VARCHAR\n    schema ANY\n    union_by_name BOOLEAN\n"}
```

```R
        filter(total_amount > 0) |>

        summarise(avg_tip_pct = mean(tip_pct), n = n(), .by = c(dn, hr)) |>

    out
}
```

If a user has a duckdb database with tables that are potentially 20GB large, it could be useful to queries those tables in duckplyr without any intermediate materialization. Some easy steps to reproduce
```
library(duckdb)
library(duckplyr)

conflict_prefer("filter", "duckplyr")

con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb("test.db"))
dbExecute(con, "create table foo as select range a from range(5000)")
rel_foo <- duckdb:::rel_from_table(con, "foo") 
altrep_df_foo <- duckdb:::rel_to_altrep(rel_foo)
duckdb:::df_is_materialized(altrep_df_foo)
# FALSE
duckplyr_df_foo <- as_duckplyr_df(altrep_df_foo)
duckplyr_df_foo %>% explain()
filtered <- duckplyr_df_foo %>% filter(a > 4999)
```

title: error in macOS: IOException - Could not remove tempfile
description:
Hi all, thanks for such an excellent package! I'm using {duckplyr} as a dependency in my package [{censobr}](https://ipeagit.github.io/censobr/) and it works super nicely but it generates [this strange error in my cmd-checks for macOS ](https://github.com/ipeaGIT/censobr/actions/runs/9974058335/job/27560749084). The error only occurs in macOS.

> Error: Error: R CMD check found ERRORs
Execution halted
180.900 129.583 310.242 
libc++abi: terminating due to uncaught exception of type duckdb::IOException: {"exception_type":"IO","exception_message":"Could not remove file \".tmp/duckdb_temp_storage-0.tmp\": No such file or directory","errno":"2"}
>
> 1 error ✖ | 0 warnings ✔ | 0 notes ✔
> Error: Process completed with exit code 1.

The error seems to occur when GithubActions checks this function:

```
censobr::read_population(year = 2000,
                         merge_households = TRUE)
```

Internally, this is what the function is doing. It (1) opens two `.parquet` files using arrow, (2) converts them to duckdb, (3) performs a left join, and (4) converts the result back to arrow.

```
library(censobr)
library(duckplyr)
library(dplyr)

df <- censobr::read_population(year = 2000)
df_household <- censobr::read_households(year = 2000)

key_vars <- c('code_muni', 'code_state', 'abbrev_state','name_state',
              'code_region', 'name_region', 'code_weighting', 'V0300')

# drop repeated vars
all_common_vars <- names(df)[names(df) %in% names(df_household)]
vars_to_drop <- setdiff(all_common_vars, key_vars)
df_household <- dplyr::select(df_household, -all_of(vars_to_drop))

# convert to duckdb
df <- arrow::to_duckdb(df)
df_household <- arrow::to_duckdb(df_household)

# merge
df_geo <- duckplyr::left_join(df, df_household)

# back to arrow
df_geo <- arrow::to_arrow(df_geo)

```

```
library(arrow)

arrow1 <- arrow::open_dataset('temp_parquet1.parquet')

# simple function that emulates part of what I do in my package
merge_fun <- function(arrow1, arrow2){

  key_vars <- c('code_muni', 'code_state', 'abbrev_state','name_state',
                'code_region', 'name_region', 'code_weighting', 'V0300')

  # drop repeated vars
  all_common_vars <- names(arrow1)[names(arrow1) %in% names(arrow2)]
  vars_to_drop <- setdiff(all_common_vars, key_vars)
  arrow2 <- dplyr::select(arrow2, -all_of(vars_to_drop)) |>
    dplyr::compute()

  # convert to duckdb
  arrow1 <- arrow::to_duckdb(arrow1)
  arrow2 <- arrow::to_duckdb(arrow2)

  # merge
  df_merge <- duckplyr::left_join(arrow1, arrow2) |>
            dplyr::compute()

  df_merge <- arrow::to_arrow(df_merge)

# run function
```

```
con <- duckplyr:::get_default_duckdb_connection()
dbExecute(con, "SET preserve_insertion_order = false;")
```

title: Remove {styler} dependency
description:
Hi, author of the formatting package {styler} here. As I judge from a search in your source code, there is no functionality that uses {styler}, in other words {styler} is not a runtime dependency. It's only used in your test that setup to deactivate the cache (I don't know why you use it there), so it's currently a test dependency. Adding {styler} as a dependency (via `Imports:` or `Suggests`:) to your package has the following drawbacks:

* Your user's may install a package they don't need (assuming most people who install your package are useres, not developers). This costs additional bandwith, installation time, disk space etc... If they need it, they can just manually install it.
* I as a maintainer of {styler} have to run reverse dependency checks (R CMD Check your package with my new version of {styler}) upon submitting to CRAN e.g. with {revdepcheck}. {styler} has more than 40 reverse dependencies, which makes this a long process.

For that reason, I suggest you to drop that dependency from your package. I.e. remove that `styler::cache_deactivate()` call that I don't get why it's there). If you want to ensure your code remains styled, I recommend {precommit} to apply {styler} on each commit or other tools described in the  [third-party integrations](https://styler.r-lib.org/articles/third-party-integrations.html) website of {styler}.

For the removal to take effect, a CRAN submission of your package is required (but the issue is not urgent). For tracking, this issue is referenced in https://github.com/r-lib/styler/issues/1121.

title: Column attribute round-tripping is too strict for datetimes
description:
A date time value without a set timezone (ex: value from `Sys.time()`) gains a timezone attribute in the duckdb conversion, thus failing the check for attribute round-tripping:

```r
library(duckplyr)

df <- data.frame(datetime = Sys.time())
attributes(df$datetime)
#> $class
#> [1] "POSIXct" "POSIXt"

as_duckdb_tibble(df)
#> Error in `duckdb_rel_from_df()`:
#> ! Attributes are lost during conversion. Affected column: `datetime`.

lubridate::tz(df$datetime) <- "UTC"
attributes(df$datetime)
#> $class
#> [1] "POSIXct" "POSIXt" 
#> 
#> $tzone
#> [1] "UTC"

as_duckdb_tibble(df)
#> # A duckplyr data frame: 1 variable
#>   datetime           
#>   <dttm>             
#> 1 2025-02-07 09:37:25
```

It seems to me that the check `!identical(df_attrib, roundtrip_attrib)` is too strict. I'm actually surprised by the `identical()` requirement here, especially when the error message is about attributes being _dropped_, which is not the case in the reprex.

https://github.com/tidyverse/duckplyr/blob/097102f5f99036493bebbf1cf21faff18335f649/R/relational-duckdb.R#L190-L196

---

Relatedly -- and I can open a separate issue about this if needed -- there are also cases where duckdb can shuffle the order of attributes without changing their contents, and I wonder whether the check should let those pass (or raise a warning vs. error).

Originally posted by **mine-cetinkaya-rundel** April 2, 2025 In the [`large` vignette](https://duckplyr.tidyverse.org/dev/articles/large.html#to-duckplyr), don't fully understand what the second information point is saying: ```r readr::read_csv("a\n1", show_col_types = FALSE) |> as_duckdb_tibble() #> Error in `as_duckdb_tibble()` at duckplyr/R/ducktbl.R:81:3: #> ! The input is data read by readr, and duckplyr supports #> reading CSV files directly. #> ℹ Use `read_csv_duckdb()` to read with the built-in reader. #> ℹ To proceed with the data as read by readr, use `as_tibble()` before #> `as_duckdb_tibble()`. ``` When I read in with `readr()` it's already a tibble, why would I need to " use `as_tibble()` before `as_duckdb_tibble()`"?

title: Reuse already materialized data frames
description:
We want to reuse `df2` once it's materialized.

In duckdb, need a new `AltrepDataFrameRelation` that wraps an ALTREP data frame and forwards to either the parent relation or to a relation that implements the data frame scan.

``` r

library(duckplyr)
#> Loading required package: dplyr
#> ✔ Overwriting dplyr methods with duckplyr methods.
#> ℹ Turn off with `duckplyr::methods_restore()`.

df1 <- duck_tbl(a = 1)
df2 <- df1 |> mutate(b = 2)
df3 <- df2 |> filter(b == 2)

duckdb:::rel_from_altrep_df(df2)
#> DuckDB Relation: 
#> ---------------------
#> --- Relation Tree ---
#> ---------------------
#> Projection [a as a, 2.0 as b]
#>   r_dataframe_scan(0x115848e88)
#> 
#> ---------------------
#> -- Result Columns  --
#> ---------------------
#> - a (DOUBLE)
#> - b (DOUBLE)
duckdb:::rel_from_altrep_df(df3)
#> DuckDB Relation: 
#> ---------------------
#> --- Relation Tree ---
#> ---------------------

#>     r_dataframe_scan(0x115848e88)
#> 
#> ---------------------
#> -- Result Columns  --

collect(df2)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
```

description:
> Hi, thank you so much for creating this package. You won't believe how long I've been waiting for something like `duckplyr`, experimenting with `data.table`, databases (do you remember Monet.DB?), and even Apache Spark. I started building science tools on top of `ducklpyr` already, and I'm extremely glad the way it turned out. Fantastic job!
> 
> I want to continue this issue discussion to make sure I clearly understand this `duckplyr` feature status as of today. My use case is relatively straightforward – the duckplyr-based data structure should have a feature to find similar strings stored in it using a user-provided vector of target strings, both regex and hamming/Levenshtein distance.
> 
> Please correct me if I'm wrong, but as of today, it is possible only via running two `compute(name=...)` -s, one for the source data, one for the target data, and then executing `read_sql_duckdb("execute levenshtein SQL code here"`). Non-reproducible example:
> 
> ```r
> source_table <- my_data_structure_on_duckplyr |>
>   compute(name = "source_table")
> 
> pattern_vec <- c("ASSSRDALNIQY", <more patterns>)
> pattern_table <- duckdb_tibble(pattern = pattern_vec) |> 
>   compute(name = "pattern_table")
> 
> query <- "
>   SELECT
>     s.seq_id,
>     s.sequence,
>     p.patterns,
>     levenshtein(s.sequence, p.pattern) AS edit_distance
>   FROM source_table s
>   CROSS JOIN pattern_table p
>   WHERE edit_distance <= <threshold>
> "
> 
> found_matches <- read_sql_duckdb(query)
>

> ```
> 
> Another possible use case is concatenating several string columns together to form a new column.
> 
> If this is correct, I'm a bit worried about the data duplication due to the first `compute(name = "source_table")`. Does #650 aim to fix this? I personally would be more than fine if I could execute an arbitrary SQL code without copying the data.
> 
> How would you remove those "temporary" tables from the duckdb instance from the current duckplyr-based session? Again, I would be more than satisfied if I could just connect to the duckdb instance and do some housekeeping.

> Thank you again (:

title: Add optional telemetry
description:
We want to know which query types are triggering a fallback to dplyr. For this, we want to collect the structure of the tables involved (with anonymized column names) and the actual query sent (only the failing part). We will post this anonymized data to an endpoint, using a variant of the following code:

```r
print(httr::content(httr::POST('https://duckplyr-telemetry.duckdblabs.com/', httr::content_type('text/plain'), body=si, encode='raw')))
```

The response is a handle that allows us to identify the request.

The telemetry will be completely opt-in, users will have to set an option to enable it. The first time a fallback occurs, users will see a prompt that allows them to share, opt-in permanently, or opt-out permanently.

title: Filters are not pushed into httpfs requests
description:
Just writing down something I noticed that we should fix eventually. 

Duckdb has the ability to query s3 buckets, and push down filters into [hive partitions](https://duckdb.org/docs/guides/import/s3_import.html). Thought this might be a cool feature to test in duckplyr since we export table functions. The s3 bucket I'm testing on contains a copy of the parquet files found here https://github.com/Tmonster/duckplyr_demo/tree/main/taxi-data-2019-partitioned. In total it's about 2.7 GB.

If I only want December data, the query
`select * from read_parquet('s3://duckplyr-demo-taxi-data/taxi-data-2019-partitioned/*/*.parquet', hive_partitioning=TRUE) where month=12` will only download data in the directory month=12

This functionality works with the regular R duckdb package. Steps to reproduce are below. 

First build R with static extensions
```bash
cd duckdb
make clean
GEN=ninja EXTENSION_STATIC_BUILD=1 BUILD_R=1 make
```
When creating a connection, we want to allow unsigned extensions for development purposes
```R
library(duckdb)
set_keys <- "set s3_region='{{region}}';set s3_access_key_id='{{access_key_id}}';set s3_secret_access_key='{{secret_access_key}}';"
DBI::dbExecute(con, set_keys)
[1] 0
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(config=list("allow_unsigned_extensions"="true")))
load_httpfs <- "LOAD '{{home_dir}}/duckdb/build/release/extension/httpfs/httpfs.duckdb_extension'"
DBI::dbExecute(con, load_httpfs)
[1] 0
dbExecute(con, "create table december as select * from read_parquet('s3://duckplyr-demo-taxi-data/taxi-data-2019-partitioned/*/*.parquet', hive_partitioning=TRUE) where month=12")
# [1] 6895933
```

The duckplyr package seems to run out of memory and hit vector exhaustion
```R
library(duckplyr)
# I modified a local version of duckplyr to automatically add the secret key etc.
taxi_data_2019_december <- duckplyr_df_from_file('s3://duckplyr-demo-taxi-data/taxi-data-2019-partitioned/*/*.parquet', 'read_parquet', list(hive_partitioning=TRUE)) |> filter(month == 12)
Error: vector memory exhausted (limit reached?)
```
If the error doesn't occur, the time it takes for the query to complete is noticeably longer than the examples in R or duckdb.

Writing out the query in the relational api works as well.
```R
library(duckdb)
set_keys <- "set s3_region='{{region}}';set s3_access_key_id='{{access_key_id}}';set s3_secret_access_key='{{secret_access_key}}';"
DBI::dbExecute(con, set_keys)
[1] 0
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(config=list("allow_unsigned_extensions"="true")))
load_httpfs <- "LOAD '{{home_dir}}/duckdb/build/release/extension/httpfs/httpfs.duckdb_extension'"
DBI::dbExecute(con, load_httpfs)
DBI::dbExecute(con, "CREATE OR REPLACE MACRO eq(a, b) AS a = b")
all_taxi_data <- duckdb:::rel_from_table_function(con, "read_parquet", list("s3://duckplyr-demo-taxi-data/taxi-data-2019-partitioned/*/*.parquet"), list(hive_partitioning=TRUE))
december_data <- duckdb:::rel_filter(all_taxi_data, list(duckdb:::expr_function("eq", list(duckdb:::expr_reference("month"), duckdb:::expr_constant(12)))))
duckdb:::rel_to_altrep(december_data)
```

Since the raw R package works and the relational package, I think this issue is somewhere in duckplyr

title: Can you explain how you translate R expressions into duckdb syntax?
description:
Hello, I'm interested in knowing the way you translate R expressions to duckdb syntax. I have a similar task to do in [`tidypolars`](https://github.com/etiennebacher/tidypolars) that aims at providing the `tidyverse` syntax for `polars`. Most functions are implemented now, but I'm not super happy with the way I translate R expressions to polars expressions in `mutate()` and `summarize()`.

Polars expressions are chained with `$`, which gives a sort of R6 syntax. To give you an example, `y = mean(x)` would be `pl$col("x")$mean()$alias("y")` in polars syntax. 

### What I do so far

I have a list of R functions with their equivalent in Polars syntax. Here's what I do so far:

* get the list of expressions in a `mutate`/`summarize` call and deparse them
* for each (deparsed) expression:
  * I get the column names (using `getParsedData`, I extract the `SYMBOL`s that match column names of the data). I wrap each column name in `pl$col()`
  * I extract function calls (still using `getParsedData`), and prefix them with `pl_`
  * in the end, `mean(x)` becomes `pl_mean(pl$col("x"))`
  * internally, I have defined `pl_mean(x)` with the `polars` syntax inside

I also have put some details in [this vignette](https://www.tidypolars.etiennebacher.com/articles/parsing-expressions). 

The main drawback of this approach is that I extract each expression as a string, which means that 1) the code relies on regular expressions and I'm far from being an expert on these, 2) it requires to `eval()` the expressions at the end. I'm not sure if the latter really is a concern, I've seen many times that `eval()` on strings is strongly discouraged but I don't know if it could lead to problematic scenarios here.

In the end, this way works but I'm curious to know if there are some alternatives to have more robust code. I tried a bit to explore the scripts in `tools` and `patch`, but I don't understand at which point you deal with this translation. Do you have some time to explain a bit the process of rewriting expressions in `duckplyr`? Or do you already have something written up somewhere? 

Thank you

title: Hash Aggregation does not preserve order
description:
I'm working on improving DuckDB's hash aggregation, and my CI runs are failing on an R test, `test-rel_api.R`, generated by `05-duckdb-tests.R`, which should not be edited by hand.

This test file includes six test cases that assume order-preserving hash aggregation:
```
"relational count() order-preserving"
"relational count(a) order-preserving"
"relational count(b) order-preserving"
"relational count(g) order-preserving"
"relational count(g, a) order-preserving"
"relational count(b, g) order-preserving"
```

DuckDB's hash aggregation does not preserve order. These test cases have succeeded for now because the tests cases meet two criteria:
1. The input size is less than 120k rows
2. There are less than 10k groups

I have made improvements to DuckDB's hash aggregation. As a result, DuckDB no longer preserves order, even if it meets these two criteria.

I would like to re-generate `test-rel_api.R` without the order-preservation checks for the hash aggregation. How would I go about doing this?

title: duckdbfs - duckplyr comparing notes
description:
Howdy friends! Just saw this (from the Posit Conf schedule!), looks amazing (though still wrapping my head around scope etc).   

I've been playing around with some possibly similar ideas in a very small wrapper package, [duckdbfs](https://github.com/cboettig/duckdbfs), because I didn't know about the efforts here.  If it makes sense, I'd be happy to merge features into here instead and archive duckdbfs.  Alternatively I'd welcome your feedback on duckdbfs

My core goal with `duckdbfs` was to have `open_dataset()`  / `write_dataset()` functions that operate like they do in arrow, (i.e. supporting local and S3 URIs), while also supporting arbitrary https urls.  (yes I know we can do things like `arrow::open_dataset() |> to_duckdb()`, but obviously that doesn't support https urls and adds overhead of using the arrow parser, which we found could be substantially slower than native duckdb httpfs mechanism).  

e.g. S3 access, with necessary config (as per #39):

```r
parquet <- "s3://gbif-open-data-us-east-1/occurrence/2023-06-01/occurrence.parquet"
gbif <- duckdbfs::open_dataset(parquet, anonymous = TRUE, s3_region="us-east-1")
```

https URIs work the same way of course.  `duckdbfs` handles installing the httpfs extension when necessary.  (Yes, it's tragic that httpfs extension still doesn't work on Windows owing to how `duckdbfs` is building those binaries!).  `duckdbfs` seeks to make the spatial extension immediately visible to R users in the same way, e.g. 


```r
library(dplyr)
spatial_ex <- paste0("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cboettig/duckdbfs/",
                     "main/inst/extdata/spatial-test.csv") |>
  duckdbfs::open_dataset(format = "csv") 

spatial_ex |>
  mutate(geometry = ST_Point(longitude, latitude)) |>
  mutate(dist = ST_Distance(geometry, ST_Point(0,0))) |> 
  to_sf()
```

Note we use `dplyr` / `dbplyr` to do lazy spatial ops, and parse the result into R as an `sf` object.
